strings.welcome.title: Welcome to ToneGrid
strings.welcome.intro: Free, open source and in private beta. Thanks for helping us improve ToneGrid!
strings.welcome.audio_intro: Select your audio interface and guitar input.
strings.welcome.windows: On Windows, use ASIO with your interface manufacturer's driver. Install it first if needed.
strings.welcome.mac: Use CoreAudio with your interface selected for input and output.
strings.welcome.linux: Use ALSA with your interface selected for input and output.
strings.welcome.calibration_copy:
Match your interface to ToneGrid's signal chain. Start with input gain at minimum and follow the guide.

Need more drive? Try AMP Gain first. Changing interface gain affects every pedal and requires recalibration.
strings.welcome.volume_copy:
Normalize balances capture levels:
OFF: original level.
Partial: capture loudness metadata.
Full: adds ToneGrid's measured correction, where available.
strings.welcome.updates_copy: Click Check for update at the bottom every 2-3 days.
strings.audio.title: Audio Settings
strings.audio.lite_help: Use lighter NAM A2 captures to reduce CPU load. Applies to compatible amp and pedal models; other captures keep their normal sound. Remembered after restarting ToneGrid.
strings.audio.calibration_help: First choose your interface and guitar input above. Then click Guitar Calibration to continue.
strings.audio.ready_help: Audio is ready. Choose the input where your guitar is plugged in, and the output connected to your speakers or headphones.
strings.audio.none_help: No audio device is open. Choose your interface and guitar input below.
strings.audio.failure:
Audio could not start: {error}
Choose your interface below to retry.
strings.audio.asio_hint: For a guitar interface, select ASIO and its manufacturer's driver when available. Windows audio remains usable.

strings.preset.user_help: Your local presets. Load, edit and save your own tones.
strings.preset.no_match: No tones match this Genre and Search.

strings.jam.no_match: No tracks match. Try All styles, All keys or a wider BPM range.

strings.learn.no_match: No lessons match. Try another filter or search.
strings.learn.title: Free Lessons
strings.learn.intro: Learn iconic songs with step-by-step guitar lessons from Guitar Club.
strings.learn.resources: Full lesson and resources on Guitar Club
strings.learn.missing_description: This video has no YouTube description. Visit Guitar Club for the full lesson and resources.
strings.record.select_help: Click anywhere in this guitar panel to select it. Render keeps its sound; Unfreeze lets you change its preset again.
strings.record.guitar_guide:
Choose a preset and record.

Click this guitar panel to select it. Play your recording and try different presets. Render applies the preset so this guitar keeps its sound while you work on the other guitar.

To change its preset later, select it and click Unfreeze. Your original recording is always kept.
strings.record.render_help: Keep this track's current sound. Later preset changes will not affect it. Your original dry recording is preserved.
strings.record.unfreeze_help: Make this track editable using its saved tone. Change the preset, then Render again. The other guitar keeps its sound.
strings.record.switch_message:
We will apply the current preset to Guitar {first} so it keeps this sound while you choose a different preset for Guitar {second}.

To change Guitar {first}'s preset later, select it and click Unfreeze. Your original recording is kept.
strings.record.zoom_in_help: Zoom in around the visible playhead, or the centre of this view.
strings.record.zoom_out_help: Zoom out to see more of the song.
strings.record.navigation_help: Drag the ruler to select time. Drag the waveforms to move the view.
strings.record.ruler_help: Click to place the cursor. Drag along this ruler to select a time range for export or Delete.
strings.record.pan_help: Drag left or right to move through the song. A click places the cursor; dragging keeps your time selection.
strings.record.mute_help: Mute this track during playback and export.
strings.record.volume_help: Track volume for playback and export. Double-click to reset.
strings.record.reference_help: Paste a YouTube link, then click Load. Video timing is approximate; its audio is excluded from exports.
strings.record.reference_note:
YouTube is a practice reference.
Timeline seeking is approximate.
Its audio is never recorded or exported.
strings.record.load_help: Copy a local MP3, WAV, FLAC or AIFF into this session as your backing track.
strings.record.remove_backing_help: Remove the local backing from this session. Your original file is preserved.
strings.record.remove_video_help: Stop the video and remove its link from this session. Guitar and local backing stay intact.
strings.record.export_all_help: Export the complete recording as an MP3, mixing both guitars and local backing. Uses track volume and mute settings. YouTube is excluded.
strings.record.export_selection_help: Export the highlighted time range as an MP3, mixing both guitars and local backing. Uses track volume and mute settings. YouTube is excluded.
strings.record.selection_first: Drag across the timeline to select a time range first.
strings.record.play_help: Play or pause at the cursor. Shortcut: Space.
strings.record.capture_help: Record dry guitar onto the track with the red recording selector.
strings.record.stop_help: Stop and finish the take. During a render or export, cancel safely.
strings.record.start_help: Return to the beginning of the timeline.
strings.play.record_help: Record the sound of ToneGrid. Click again to stop. Maximum 10 minutes.
strings.play.play_help: Play the last recording. Click again to stop.
strings.play.export_help: Export the last recording as MP3.
strings.calibration.input_reason: This setting is designed for electric guitars. Without it, your signal may sound weaker, duller, or respond differently to amps and pedals.
strings.calibration.gain_reason: Keep it there while using ToneGrid to preserve accurate NAM calibration.
strings.calibration.save_failed: Could not save. Your previous settings were kept.
strings.calibration.estimate: Estimate. Enter an exact value if known.
strings.calibration.dbu_help: dBu describes your interface's input sensitivity. It helps ToneGrid make the pedals and amps respond correctly. It is not a volume target to reach while playing.
strings.calibration.ready_copy:
Choose your audio interface and follow two simple steps.

Then play a few notes to check your input.
strings.calibration.play_copy: ToneGrid checks your guitar input. You can leave your pedals and amp on.
strings.calibration.select_audio: Select your interface in Audio Settings.
strings.calibration.check_gain: Check the input GAIN setting for your interface.
strings.calibration.no_signal: No signal detected yet. You can still save these settings.
strings.calibration.play_when_ready: Play a few notes when you're ready.
strings.calibration.connect: Connect your interface and select it in Audio Settings.
strings.calibration.channel: Choose the instrument input channel specified by this profile.
strings.calibration.plug_generic:

Enable INST / Hi-Z if available.

strings.missing.update_help: Open the download page for the latest ToneGrid. The complete package includes its Factory amps and cabinets.
strings.cab.power_help: Turn off the cabinet simulation when using a real guitar cabinet. Your amp stays active. Click again to restore the selected IR. Available with Head Only captures.
strings.cab.lock_help: Keep this IR when changing amp heads. Unlock it to follow the next head's recommended cabinet. Full Rig captures keep their included cabinet.
strings.record.delete_help: Delete the selected time range from Guitar {number}. Later audio stays in place. Unfreeze this track before editing.
strings.record.backing_guide:
Play along with a local backing track.

Load an MP3, WAV, FLAC or AIFF. It starts at 00:00 and is copied into this session. Set its volume or mute it. Remove clears the lane without changing your original file. Local backing can be included in exports.
strings.record.youtube_guide:
A video reference for practising.

Paste a YouTube link and click Load. Play or pause in ToneGrid or in the video. Moving either timeline keeps them together. ToneGrid waits for the video before starting. If the video pauses or buffers during a take, the take is saved; press Record to continue. Small timing differences can remain. YouTube sound is never recorded or exported. With exclusive ASIO, try shared audio or local backing.

strings.eq.curve_tip: Select a band, then drag its point. Arrow keys adjust gain and frequency. The curve shows the actual combined EQ response.
strings.eq.footer: Low Cut: reduce rumble. High Cut: soften harsh highs. Double-click any control to reset.
strings.eq.cut_detail: Frequency and On/Off are always available below.
strings.eq.fixed_frequency: {frequency} Hz — Fixed tone-control frequency. Adjust the knob or drag vertically.
strings.pitch.choose: Select a Pitch mode in the top bar.
strings.effects.help.1: Shifts the entire guitar signal up or down by up to two octaves. The output is fully transposed, with no dry blend.
strings.effects.help.2: Sets the original guitar level. It is delayed to match the two octave voices.
strings.effects.help.3: Sets the level of the voice one octave below your guitar.
strings.effects.help.4: Sets the level of the voice one octave above your guitar.
strings.effects.help.5: Select Transpose or Octaver in the top bar. OFF adds no pitch latency.
strings.effects.help.6: Pitch acts after the noise gate and before the thirteen pedals. Active pitch processing adds a small delay; try chords and strong attacks when checking your sound.
strings.effects.help.7: Controls the time between the original note and each repeat.
strings.effects.help.8: Controls how many repeats are generated.
strings.effects.help.9: Controls how much delayed signal is blended with the original guitar. 100% gives only the echoes.
strings.effects.help.10: Tap repeatedly to set the delay time by feel.
strings.effects.help.11: Creates clean repeating echoes of the guitar signal. Digital Delay follows MOD and comes before Reverb.
strings.effects.help.12: Controls how fast the modulation moves.
strings.effects.help.13: Controls how strong the modulation effect becomes.
strings.effects.help.14: Blends in the modulation. Tremolo Level controls the strength of the volume pulse; Chorus, Phaser and Flanger blend their moving sound with your guitar.
strings.effects.help.15: Rhythmically changes the guitar volume to create a smooth pulsing movement.
strings.effects.help.16: Creates sweeping phase cancellations for a smooth, swirling character.
strings.effects.help.17: Uses a very short modulated delay to create a more pronounced sweeping effect.
strings.effects.help.18: Adds slightly detuned, moving copies of the guitar to create width and shimmer.
strings.reverb.help.1: Shorter, natural reflections that make the guitar feel like it is playing in a real space.
strings.reverb.help.2: Smooth, dense and musical reverb with a classic studio character.
strings.reverb.help.3: Simulates the lively metallic character of a traditional spring reverb tank, with the splash and drip associated with classic guitar amplifiers.
strings.reverb.help.4: Creates a wider and deeper space with a longer, more atmospheric tail.
strings.reverb.help.5: Controls how long the spring tail rings. Start with a moderate time to keep chords clear.
strings.reverb.help.6: Moves the spring tone from warm and mellow to brighter and more present.
strings.reverb.help.7: Controls how long the reverb tail takes to fade away. Seconds are an approximate musical target, not a measured RT60.
strings.reverb.help.8: Adds a short gap before the reverb begins, helping the original guitar attack stay clear.
strings.reverb.help.9: Adjusts the tonal character of the reverb from darker and warmer to brighter and more present.
strings.reverb.help.10: Controls how much reverb is blended with the dry guitar signal. Start at 10-25% for guitar.
strings.reverb.help.11: Adds a sense of space and depth after the amplifier. Room, Plate and Large share the existing engine; Spring uses a dedicated spring tank.
strings.reverb.guide:
Time
How long the reverb tail rings.

Pre-delay
The gap before the reverb starts, keeping the guitar attack clear.

Color
From dark and warm to bright and present.

Mix
The amount of reverb blended with your dry guitar.
strings.spread.help.1: Adds a small timing difference between the left and right channels to create stereo width.
strings.spread.help.2: Adds subtle movement so the stereo image feels less static.
strings.spread.help.3: Softens and spreads transients to create a smoother, more spacious stereo image.
strings.spread.help.4: Sets the frequency above which widening becomes stronger, helping keep low frequencies focused.
strings.spread.help.5: Creates a wider, more immersive stereo image after the amp while keeping the core guitar tone focused.
